acceptance: Each new dialect has tests/dialects tests (validate_identity/validate_all); registry and enum edits are carried patches with fix: retain commits; relocate.py allowlists need no change or the change is justified.
The date-arithmetic rewrite takes column types or a schema as an argument, contains no TPC-DS names, and has execution tests on Postgres (container) proving date +/- int semantics.
DataFusion dialect output executes on the in-process datafusion package; engines not obtainable are listed in the PR against the F0b gap list.
The PR states the key space BenchBox must map (standard, ansi, netezza and each platform) so D1 can implement the mapping.
Fork make check, make benchbox-dist and make benchbox-check pass; PR merged.
description: normalize_dialect_for_sqlglot maps netezza, greenplum, vertica, datafusion and ansi/standard onto postgres in BenchBox. Callers pass 'standard' (datavault/benchmark.py:274, tpcds_obt/benchmark.py:412,421), 'ansi' (tpcdi/queries.py:203) and 'netezza' (translate_sql_query defaults). Add explicit fork dialects (thin Postgres subclasses where appropriate; QuestDB as a dialect skeleton) following the Dune pattern (dialects/, parsers/, generators/, Dialects enum, DIALECTS and MODULE_BY_DIALECT). Edits to upstream-owned registry files are carried patches per the F0 policy. This slice also creates the fork's sqlglot/benchbox/ package. The platform-to-dialect mapping lives in BenchBox's platform registry, not the fork; the fork only provides the dialects and documents how ansi/standard aliases resolve. fix_postgres_date_arithmetic is a postgres-target post-processor keyed on d_date column names, not a Netezza reader rule: expose it as a fork rewrite that takes column types or a schema as arguments, with the date-column gate data staying in BenchBox.
